headline: Learned models steer molecular design toward feasible, affinity-optimized ligands
label: Learned Molecular Representation And Design
summary: Recent work pairs reaction-aware generation with geometric docking and site-aware affinity prediction across the design pipeline.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational molecular design that couples learned representations with chemistry- or structure-aware scoring. TRACE-GFN pairs a transformer that learns chemical reactions with a GFlowNet steered by QSAR guidance, targeting DRD2, AKT1, and CXCR4. CellChem pretrains molecular embeddings on cellular transcriptional profiles so that representation distances reflect cellular responses, aiming at multi-scale drug discovery. On the structural side, CGDock uses curvature-aware geometric flows with Ricci curvature graph encoding for protein-ligand docking, while DCI-SiteDTA integrates binding site detection into drug-target affinity prediction through a site-aware dual cross-interaction block. What is new in this set is the explicit encoding of synthetic feasibility within generation in TRACE-GFN. The remaining items advance representation learning, docking, or affinity prediction rather than synthesizability itself.
